title: Ulyana and the Rivergate
premise: Coral Sterling leads a small railroad survey crew that survives by mapping lines nobody wants and staying off everyone's radar. When her old rival Ulyana Voss hires them to reopen the Rivergate line through monsoon country, Coral must choose between the crew's loyalty to their unspoken pact of invisibility and the truth about why the Rivergate was abandoned: a washout that killed Coral's mentor, a disaster the records blame on her. As the flood season closes in, the crew takes Ulyana's money, runs the river in a leaking boat with help from a stranger named Idris who knows the water better than any map, and finally confronts what really happened at the washout. In the end, Coral tells the truth at the cost of the contract, the crew chooses her over the job, and they build not the line Ulyana wanted but a smaller crossing the valley actually needs—finding belonging not by hiding, but by being known.
about_author: Beatrix Zhou is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six seasons mapping remote rail corridors before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who love difficult landscapes and the crews who become their families.

chapters.title: Lines Nobody Wants
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her crew finishes a forgotten spur survey and celebrates quietly, establishing their code: take obscure jobs, stay invisible, never look back. A telegram arrives from Ulyana Voss offering triple pay for the Rivergate. The beat is uneasy comfort—the family is warm, but the offer cracks something open.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Job
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a flashback to the washout that killed her mentor Aldous and stained her name. She refuses Ulyana's offer; the crew votes anyway, needing the money before winter. The emotional beat is betrayal edged with understanding—loyalty tested by hunger.

chapters.title: Terms of the Rival
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In her office she reveals she knows more about the washout than she should, and dangles the one thing Coral can't refuse: sealed incident records. Old rivalry masks an old debt between them. The beat is dangerous fascination—two women reading each other like terrain.

chapters.title: Downriver Contract
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew travels to the Rivergate headwaters, meeting Idris, a ferryman who warns them the monsoon is early and the boat Ulyana provided is rotten. First signs the job is a trap or a test. The beat is foreboding wrapped in bravado.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He guides them past drowned trestles and shares local memory of the washout—details that contradict the official record Coral has carried for years. Doubt takes root. The beat is quiet revelation; the wilderness remembers what paperwork buried.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Mid-river storm; the hull splits and the crew bails through the night while Ulyana's second-in-command, Marsh, sabotages the radio. Coral realizes Ulyana never intended the survey to succeed. The beat is terror forging trust among the found family.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Stranded at base camp as the river rises, she reads Aldous's real field notes and learns her own company falsified the washout report—and that Coral took the blame to protect the crew's first contract. The beat is guilt arriving too conveniently late.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax: the crew reaches the old gate structure as the flood peaks, with Marsh trying to destroy Aldous's recovered notes. Confrontation on the crumbling catwalk; Idris's knowledge of the water saves them, and Coral chooses truth over the sealed records. The beat is everything breaking open at once.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She publicly retracts the falsified report, ending her own company's claim and her rivalry with Coral—not as surrender but as repair. Marsh is dismissed; the contract dissolves. The beat is costly amends, loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: A Smaller Crossing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Epilogue in dry season: the crew, with Idris among them now, builds a modest foot-and-freight crossing the valley asked for instead of the grand line Ulyana wanted. Coral's name is cleared, but better, it's known. The beat is belonging earned in daylight.
